newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Wastewater Treatment Trust rated AAA - S&P.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Wastewater Treatment Trust rated AAA - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 2 - Standard & Poor's today has assigned its triple-A' rating to New Jersey Wastewater Treatment Trust's $47 million wastewater treatment bonds series 1996A and $5 million AMT wastewater treatment bonds series 1996B.
The rating reflects the program's following strengths:
-- Cash flow structure of a diverse and growing portfolio of borrowers meeting Standard & Poor's triple-A' pool financing criteria,
-- The subordination of the state' right to receive loan repayments to that of the trust,
-- The master trust indenture covenant to maintain the triple-A' rating on the program,
-- A program level debt service reserve funded at 10% bond proceeds and invested in triple-A' securities, and
-- Strong management oversight of the trust by the state.

Cash flows were prepared for all outstanding loans to the 90 current borrowers and additional anticipated loans through 2001. Including this bond sale, the portfolio of borrowers' credit quality consists: 10.0% triple-A' rated loans, 20.4% double-A', 9.3% single-A', 19.4% triple-B', and 40.8% not rated. No concentration penalty was applied because the largest borrower, Camden County Municipal Utility Authority, which represents about 10% of the outstanding loans, has its fund and trust loan repayments insured by FGIC. The aggregate loan payments adequately withstand a default rate of about 23% and maintain a minimum required coverage of 1.30 times, satisfying S&P's triple-A' criteria for a large pool.

The program structure consists of each participant receiving a zero interest loan from the state and a market rate loan from the trust, which together provide for a below market rate loan. Under the master trust indenture, the excess state loan repayments originated between 1990-1994 are additionally pledged as security to trust loans.

This mechanism establishes one large pool of excess cash flow, which adds a second layer of bondholder protection. In addition, the subordination the state loan repayment creates excess cash flow that enhances bond security since both repayment streams are pledged to the repayment of the bonds.

Additional factors that support the rating include each local government borrower's pledge of its full faith and credit to the repayment of the loans. Moreover, each utility authority borrower has service contracts with the communities they serve that are G.O. pledges of the respective communities, have funded a separate debt service reserve, and have placed loan repayments on parity with their respective outstanding debt. In addition, the trust has the authority to intercept state aid of a borrower should it fail to repay its obligations.
The outlook reflects the program structure and current and projected diverse credit profile of pool borrowers, Standard & Poor's said.
